note: Faithful rendering of the Lotus verses, the burning-house and conjured-city parables and the Satyaka-parivarta citation; nothing of substance to change.

errors.english: if that which is empty of appearances is another property
errors.why: The verse says another property that is empty of the semblance of that (i.e. free of being a pseudo-reason) would equally become a reason; 'empty of appearances' loses the hetvābhāsa sense.

errors.english: Others qualify the former as that which performs the proof for the (sādhya) the thesis or that which is to be proven.
errors.why: Others qualify 'being the prover of the probandum' by means of the former (similarity of property), as the following quotation shows; the English inverts what qualifies what.

errors.english: this is a matter that is certain in the way of knowledge as being the sixth category
errors.why: དྲུག་པ here is the sixth (genitive) grammatical case, not a sixth ontological category.

note: Follows the Tibetan sentence by sentence but blurs several points of the logical argument (pseudo-reason, qualification, grammatical case); the Pramāṇa reasoning needs a careful pass.

errors.english: The Buddha then commanded (Ananda) the Buddha's cousin and personal attendant
errors.why: དགའ་བོ is Nanda, not Ānanda (ཀུན་དགའ་བོ); the same misidentification recurs in 'Ananda sent the monk Lamten' and 'reported this conversation to Ananda'.

fix.find: The Buddha then commanded (Ananda) the Buddha's cousin and personal attendant

errors.english: She met a novice going to Shravasti
errors.why: The Tibetan says a bhikṣu (fully ordained monk), not a novice; the rule concerns monks.

fix.find: She met a novice going to Shravasti
fix.replace: She met a monk going to Shravasti

note: Vinaya rule and origin story are rendered in substance, but the key figure Nanda is turned into Ānanda throughout and the monk becomes a novice.

errors.english: If one posits the otherness of distinct continua as the ultimate reason
errors.why: དོན་དམ་པར is adverbial: if one ultimately (in the ultimate sense) posits the otherness of distinct continua as the reason, not 'the ultimate reason'.

note: Sound rendering of the objection on the reason and example and Bhāviveka's reply that the reason is stated generally.

errors.english: Since there is no birth, there is no permanence. In this context, if something were to be born, it would be permanent; but since that is not the case, there is no permanence. Because there is no cessation
errors.why: The Tibetan goes straight from 'no birth is mentioned after no cessation' to 'because there is no cessation there is no annihilation'; the no-birth/no-permanence sentence is inserted here and then repeated in its proper place.

fix.find: "no birth" is mentioned immediately after "no cessation." Since there is no birth, there is no permanence. In this context, if something were to be born, it would be permanent; but since that is not the case, there is no permanence. Because there is no cessation
fix.replace: "no birth" is mentioned immediately after "no cessation." Because there is no cessation

note: The Prajñāpāramitā dialogue and the commentary on the order of the negations are accurate, apart from one duplicated sentence.

errors.english: preceded by the doubts of the (tirthikas) non-Buddhist extremists, the noble (shravakas), and the (bodhisattvas) respectively
errors.why: ལ marks the tīrthikas, śrāvakas and bodhisattvas as the ones analysed by the three qualifications, with doubts raised regarding each, not as the ones who hold the doubts.

note: Generally sound commentary on compassion and habituation as grounds of the Buddha's authority; the closing sentence is a little garbled.
The argument about Jaimini and supersensible knowledge is rendered correctly; the opening sentence is awkward but follows a difficult Tibetan.
Faithful rendering of the Tibetan verses of the Anaṅgaṇa story, with the interleaved Sanskrit set aside in notes.

errors.english: You who possess excellent knowledge do not accept that only some people are knowledgeable.
errors.why: The Tibetan asks the opponent why he does not accept that someone is endowed with superior knowledge; 'you' is not the possessor of the knowledge.

fix.find: You who possess excellent knowledge do not accept that only some people are knowledgeable.
fix.replace: Why do you not accept that someone is endowed with superior knowledge?

errors.english: you all must grasp this meaning of mine; no one else shall.
errors.why: གཞན་ནི་མ་ཡིན means 'not another [meaning]': the Veda would have to say 'this is my meaning, not another one'.

fix.find: you all must grasp this meaning of mine; no one else shall.
fix.replace: you all must grasp this meaning of mine, not any other.

errors.english: a sound that is connected to a meaning of ignorance itself
errors.why: The point is a sound connected with an unknown (undetermined) meaning, not with a meaning that is 'ignorance'.

errors.english: they must be certain for one person
errors.why: The objection is that words are restricted to a single meaning, not certain for one person.

note: The anti-Mīmāṃsā argument on the indeterminacy of Vedic meaning is recognisable, but several referents are confused, starting with the opening sentence.

errors.english: Death is like the tracks of a wolf [note: leaving nothing behind]
errors.why: The wolf's footprint alludes to the Lokāyata parable of faked wolf tracks (claims about the hereafter are deceptive inference), not to death leaving nothing behind.

note: Accurate rendering of the Nāgārjuna, Āryadeva and sūtra citations and the Cārvāka verse; only the explanatory note on the wolf track misleads.
